introduction: Two routes keep a workspace and its remote in step: a sync that brings the remote's work in, with six distinct outcomes, and a branch push that sends one branch back out under eight ordered checks. A reclone recovers a repository that is beyond repair without losing commits that exist only inside Parley.

glossary.branch push: Sending exactly one branch of the workspace's repository to origin with the workspace's stored credential, fast-forward only unless force is given.
glossary.diverged origin: An origin whose head does not descend from the workspace's local head, usually because someone force-pushed. It is refused rather than merged, and recovered with reset_to_upstream.
glossary.protected branch: The workspace's own branch, which this route refuses to force-push.
glossary.reclone: Discarding a workspace's repository and copying it again, after first pushing out what branches it can, as the last resort for a repository that cannot be repaired.
glossary.sync outcome: One of the six results of a standard sync: up to date, fast-forward, reset, diverged, fetch failure, or cancelled. Each has its own status and its own effect on the workspace's fields.

requirements.title: The outcomes of a standard sync
requirements.rationale: A client distinguishes recoverable divergence from a failed fetch by the status and the recorded error, and conflating them hides the recovery.

criteria.condition: a sync runs on a standard workspace
criteria.guard: origin's head equals the workspace's local head
criteria.action: report the workspace as up to date and record the time
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the workspace; last_sync_at is the time of this sync; head_sha is unchanged and sync_error is null

criteria.condition: a sync runs on a standard workspace
criteria.guard: origin's head descends from the workspace's local head
criteria.action: fast-forward the workspace's branch to origin's head
criteria.contract: HTTP 200; head_sha and upstream_head_sha both equal origin's head; last_sync_at is updated and sync_error is null

criteria.condition: a sync runs with reset_to_upstream true on a standard workspace
criteria.guard: origin's head differs from the workspace's local head
criteria.action: move the workspace's branch to origin's head whatever the ancestry
criteria.contract: HTTP 200; head_sha and upstream_head_sha equal origin's head even where origin's head does not descend from the previous local head; sync_error is null

criteria.condition: origin's head does not descend from the workspace's local head and reset_to_upstream was not given
criteria.action: refuse the sync and record how to recover
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 in the error envelope; sync_error is set and names reset_to_upstream as the recovery; head_sha is unchanged

criteria.condition: the fetch from origin fails, or the credentials cannot be resolved
criteria.action: refuse the sync and record the failure
criteria.contract: HTTP 502 in the error envelope; sync_error is set and contains no credential; head_sha and upstream_head_sha are unchanged

criteria.condition: a sync is cancelled part way, by a timeout or a disconnected client
criteria.action: end the sync and record that it was cancelled
criteria.contract: HTTP 504 in the error envelope; sync_error is set; the workspace is left in a state a retry recovers from

criteria.condition: a sync succeeds after an earlier one failed
criteria.action: clear the recorded sync error
criteria.contract: sync_error is null after the successful sync, so the field describes the present condition rather than a history

requirements.title: When a sync may run
requirements.rationale: A sync writes the repository, so the preconditions are what stop two of them colliding or one running against a repository that does not exist.

criteria.condition: a sync is called on a workspace that is not ready, or whose sync_enabled setting is false
criteria.action: refuse it and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 in the error envelope; no fetch is attempted and no workspace field changes

criteria.condition: a sync finds another operation holding the workspace's lock
criteria.action: refuse it at once rather than waiting
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_busy; the same sync succeeds once the lock is free

criteria.action: treat a sync in progress as the holding of the lock and not as a stored status
criteria.contract: the workspace's status stays ready throughout a sync; a second concurrent sync is refused by the lock

requirements.title: Recloning a workspace
requirements.rationale: It is the last resort for an unusable repository, and it must not be the operation that loses the commits it was meant to rescue.

criteria.condition: a reclone is called on a workspace that is not archived and has no copy under way
criteria.action: push what branches it can to origin, discard the repository, clear the sync fields and copy the repository again
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the workspace at status pending, sync_error null and upstream_head_sha null; the status then follows the new copy to ready or failed

criteria.condition: the reclone's push to origin fails, or there is no usable credential
criteria.action: carry on with the reclone regardless
criteria.contract: the reclone still answers 200 with status pending and the repository is copied again; the push failure does not surface as the route's answer

criteria.condition: a reclone is called on an archived workspace, on one whose copy is already under way, or while the workspace's lock is held
criteria.action: refuse it and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 for an archived workspace, HTTP 409 for a copy under way, HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_busy for a held lock; the repository is untouched

criteria.condition: the repository cannot be discarded, or the workspace cannot be updated
criteria.action: refuse the reclone
criteria.contract: HTTP 500 in the error envelope; the workspace keeps its previous status and repository

requirements.title: The branch push's checks, in order
requirements.rationale: Every refusal here can be produced for the wrong reason, and only the order distinguishes a correct implementation from one that happens to agree on simple cases.

criteria.action: check the credential, then a personal access token's workspaces:write before the workspace is looked up, then the workspace and write access, then the body, then the branch name, then that the workspace is ready, then the branches it will not push, then the workspace lock without waiting
criteria.contract: for each pair of conditions that would both fail, the answer is the one belonging to the earlier check; a PAT without the scope gets 403 even for a slug that names nothing

criteria.action: take the branch name from one path segment, decoded exactly once
criteria.contract: fix%2F42-nil-map names fix/42-nil-map and a%2525b names a%25b; a name with an unescaped slash matches no route and is 404

criteria.condition: the branch name breaks git's branch-name rules or starts with a hyphen
criteria.action: refuse the request, naming the rule broken
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with error_type branch_not_found and a message beginning "branch_not_found: " and naming the rule

criteria.condition: the workspace's status is not ready, or the body is not a JSON object or carries a non-boolean force
criteria.action: refuse the request and push nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 in the error envelope; an empty body, {} and a body with unknown fields are all accepted and push without force

criteria.condition: the branch is a carry_patch workspace's integration branch, a registered patch that is not deleted, or — with force — the workspace's own branch
criteria.action: refuse the request and push nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with error_type integration_branch, patch_branch or protected_branch respectively; the answer is the same whether or not the workspace's lock is held

criteria.condition: the branch push finds the workspace's lock held
criteria.action: refuse it at once rather than waiting
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_busy

criteria.condition: force is given and the workspace has no branch set and the name is the branch HEAD points to, or the repository has no such branch
criteria.action: refuse the request and push nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with error_type protected_branch for the HEAD branch; HTTP 404 with error_type branch_not_found and the message naming the branch for one the repository lacks

requirements.title: What a branch push answers
requirements.rationale: afc prints the result verbatim, and a push that reports the wrong result tells an operator a branch reached the forge when it did not.

criteria.condition: a branch push succeeds
criteria.action: answer with the branch, the commit offered, the remote and its URL, and the result
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with branch, sha as the 40-character tip offered to origin, remote "origin", remote_url and result

criteria.action: report result as up_to_date when origin already had the commit and nothing was sent, forced when force was given and origin accepted an update, and pushed otherwise
criteria.contract: pushing an unchanged branch again reports up_to_date, including with force; a forced update origin accepts reports forced

criteria.action: report remote_url as git_url without its userinfo, leaving an scp-style address unchanged
criteria.contract: an https URL carrying userinfo is reported without it; git@host:path is reported exactly as stored

criteria.condition: the caller of a branch push disconnects while the push is running
criteria.action: run the push to its end or its two-minute deadline and record its outcome as if the caller were there
criteria.contract: the branch's state on origin after the disconnect is the same as it would have been had the caller waited; calling the route again reports where the branch stands

requirements.title: How a branch push fails
requirements.rationale: afc shows only the message, so the error type has to be in it, and nothing in it may be a credential.

criteria.condition: origin's branch has commits the workspace's branch lacks
criteria.action: refuse the push and say how to proceed
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error_type non_fast_forward; the message names origin's commit when origin's refs could be listed and ends with an instruction to push with force, or to sync the workspace when the branch is the workspace's own; where force was given and origin still refused, it says origin refuses non-fast-forward updates even with force

criteria.condition: origin has no such repository or the credential cannot see it, or origin refuses the ref
criteria.action: refuse the push with the matching type
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with error_type forge_not_found for the first; HTTP 422 with error_type forge_rejected for the second, carrying origin's scrubbed reason

criteria.condition: origin answers 401 or 403, the connection fails, origin answers in a way the service cannot read, or the two-minute deadline passes
criteria.action: refuse the push with the matching type
criteria.contract: HTTP 502 with error_type forge_unauthenticated, forge_forbidden, forge_unreachable or forge_error as applicable, and HTTP 504 with error_type forge_timeout at the deadline; forge_unauthenticated says whether the workspace has no stored credential or which kind origin rejected

criteria.action: begin the message of any answer carrying one of this route's own error types with that type followed by a colon and a space
criteria.contract: for each of this route's error types the message starts with "<type>: "; answers shared with other routes keep their usual messages

criteria.action: keep the credential, the userinfo of git_url and the underlying git error out of every answer of both routes
criteria.contract: no response body of a sync, a reclone or a branch push contains the credential, userinfo, or the git transport's own error text

execution_paths.title: A sync brings the remote's new commits in

steps.action: calls the sync route on a standard workspace whose origin has advanced
takes the workspace lock and resolves the origin credential from the workspace's secrets
fetches origin and fast-forwards the workspace's branch in the repository
holds the advanced branch
receives the workspace with head_sha and upstream_head_sha at origin's head, last_sync_at set and sync_error null

execution_paths.title: A rewritten origin is refused and then recovered

steps.action: syncs a workspace whose origin was force-pushed
finds origin's head does not descend from the local head, records the sync error and answers 409
reads the workspace and sees sync_error naming reset_to_upstream
syncs again with reset_to_upstream
moves the branch to origin's head, clears sync_error and answers 200

execution_paths.title: An agent's branch is pushed to the forge

steps.action: pushes a branch whose name contains a slash to Parley's git server
calls the branch push route with that name as one escaped path segment
runs its checks in order, takes the lock and resolves the origin credential
accepts the branch at the offered commit
receives result pushed with the branch, the SHA offered and the remote URL without userinfo
calls the reclone route on a workspace whose repository is unusable
pushes what branches it can to origin, then discards the repository and clears the sync fields
copies the repository again and answers 200 with status pending
holds the freshly copied repository
polls the workspace and finds it ready again
